summary: Crawford withdrawal was improper because the appeal was not wholly frivolous. De novo Appellate Division review was required because potentially meritorious constitutional and counsel-performance claims remained.
People's appeal was dismissed under CPL 450.90. Appellate Division reversal was not on the law alone.
Conflict and trial-error claims did not establish entitlement to reversal. Conviction affirmed because the identified defects did not undermine verdict reliability.
Extreme emotional disturbance charge did not require CPL 250.10 notice on these facts. New trial required because the defense was erroneously withheld from the jury.
Accomplice-liability proof was legally sufficient for robbery and felony-murder counts. Rational inferences from coordinated conduct and stolen proceeds supported the verdict.
Unlawful-surveillance conviction was supported by legally sufficient proof. Surreptitious recording in a private setting satisfied the statutory elements.
Sua sponte competency inquiry before granting self-representation was not constitutionally required on this record. No objective indicia showed defendant lacked capacity to proceed pro se.
Robbery conviction was affirmed. Statutory forcible-stealing element was satisfied under the proof credited by the trier of fact.
Order reversed and matter remitted. Record errors required renewed proceedings in Supreme Court.
Missing scratch-report evidence did not compel an adverse-inference charge. Trial court discretion was properly exercised because prejudice was not shown.
Grand-jury integrity was not impaired by the prosecutor's handling of a requested witness. Dismissal was unwarranted because any missteps were isolated and nonprejudicial.

Defendant's inculpatory statements were involuntary under governing due-process standards. Suppression and a new trial were required because interrogation tactics created an unacceptable risk of false incrimination.
Appeal was dismissed for lack of CPL 450.90 jurisdiction. Appellate Division modification was not reviewable as a law-only determination.
Antommarchi waiver was valid. Record showed a knowing relinquishment of presence rights for sidebar voir dire questioning.
Confession-corroboration challenge failed under CPL 60.50. Independent proof sufficiently connected defendant to the criminal conduct.

Search of a closed purse incident to arrest was unconstitutional without proven exigency. Suppression required because People failed to show a reasonable basis for immediate weapon or evidence-protection concerns.
Forcible touching covers intentional pressure contact with sexual or intimate parts. Statutory text does not require the narrower physical-contact theory urged by defendant.
CPL 440 ineffective-assistance motion required further fact development. Remittal was necessary because papers raised nonfrivolous disputes about counsel's strategic justification.
Corrective resentencing to add PRS did not violate double jeopardy in this posture. Original sentence was illegal and remained subject to lawful correction.
Misdemeanor accusatory instrument was facially sufficient. Evidentiary allegations established reasonable cause for the charged licensing offense.
Accomplice-in-fact instruction was required. Evidence permitted a finding that the key witness participated in the crime, so omission was not harmless.
Search was invalid because the predicate arrest lacked probable cause. Suppression required and indictment dismissed as fruit of the unlawful arrest.

Long-dormant appeals may be dismissed in the Appellate Division's discretion without constitutional violation in appropriate circumstances. One companion case required remittal for counsel-assisted opposition before dismissal.
CPL 30.30 chargeable time exceeded the statutory limit. Information dismissed because prosecution readiness was untimely.
Second-degree manslaughter charge was properly denied. No reasonable view of the evidence supported a merely reckless mental state.
Verdict-sheet challenge under CPL 310.20 failed. Any constitutional error from warrantless GPS placement was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt.
Access to complainant's psychiatric records was properly denied after in camera review. Trial court's balancing of confrontation interests and confidentiality was within discretion.
Forfeiture-by-wrongdoing doctrine permitted admission of grand-jury testimony. Record support existed for finding defendant procured the witness's unavailability.

Gursey right to counsel was violated by administering a chemical test without notifying defendant of counsel's telephonic intervention. Suppression was proper because no unreasonable interference with testing was shown.
Evidence was legally insufficient for first-degree criminal contempt. Appellate Division affirmance of dismissal was sustained.
Enterprise-corruption review applied an incorrect legal framework. Remittal required for Appellate Division analysis under the proper statutory-elements standard.
Pure legal sufficiency argument preserved by pretrial motion need not be repeated in a trial dismissal motion. Resisting-arrest conviction was unsupported once the underlying arrest was unlawful.

Criminal impersonation statute requires intended injury or benefit of legally cognizable substance, including reputational injury in proper circumstances. Aggravated-harassment counts failed constitutional scrutiny and several convictions were vacated for overbreadth or statutory mismatch.
Defendant validly waived prosecution by information. Misdemeanor complaint allegations met facial-sufficiency requirements for the charged obstruction theory.
Plea-withdrawal claim was preserved by presentence challenge to voluntariness and innocence. Plea vacatur was required because record did not establish a knowing and voluntary admission.
Appellate Division erred in disturbing the conviction on the ground it chose. Judgment was reinstated and unresolved factual issues were remitted to that court.

Defense retrograde-BAC opinion below the per se threshold is not prima facie proof of non-intoxication on common-law DWI. Jury could credit observational intoxication evidence notwithstanding expert disagreement.

Defendant's absence from a one-juror supplemental instruction was not reversible mode-of-proceedings error under the circumstances presented. Core fairness interests were not fatally compromised on this record.

SORA factor 3 may be scored using the number of children depicted in child-pornography files. Downward departures require defendant proof by a preponderance and are not compelled by policy disagreement alone.
Robbery intent to retain stolen property can be proved without physical recovery of the property from defendant. Force used to overcome resistance during retention phase satisfies the statute.

Failure to provide meaningful notice of a substantive jury note required vacatur of the manslaughter conviction. Error did not taint the separate weapon count because the note concerned homicide elements only.
Burglary convictions were supported by legally sufficient proof of unlawful entry and contemporaneous criminal intent. Appellate challenge to element proof was rejected.

Syville coram nobis relief is limited to rare situations lacking any other procedural avenue. Relief was unavailable where defendants had or used CPL 460.30 remedies or sought discretionary leave review outside Syville's scope.
Loaded-firearm possession plus statutory presumption supported intent element under Penal Law 265.03(1)(b). Legal sufficiency challenge failed.
People's appeal was dismissed for lack of CPL 450.90 jurisdiction. Appellate Division determination was not a reviewable law-only reversal.
Padilla noncitizen-advice rule is not retroactive in New York collateral review for pre-Padilla pleas. Postconviction vacatur was therefore unavailable under the asserted theory.
Best-evidence rule did not bar testimonial proof identifying source of stolen funds under this record. Conviction affirmed because no foundational document-production requirement was triggered.

Undisclosed civil allegations against a detective in an unrelated case did not establish Brady materiality here. Hearing order was reversed because the claimed impeachment value was too attenuated from trial reliability.

Depraved-indifference murder conviction was legally insufficient in a vehicular police-chase homicide. Conduct established grave recklessness but not the requisite utter disregard for human life under narrowed doctrine.

County cyberbullying local law was facially overbroad under the First Amendment. Criminal prohibition swept substantial protected expression and could not be narrowed by judicial severance as proposed.
Coram nobis relief was warranted to permit a late notice of appeal. Defendant satisfied the narrow ineffective-assistance framework for restoration of first-tier appellate rights.
Suppression and trial-fairness claims did not warrant reversal. Remaining sufficiency and misconduct arguments were unpreserved.
Exigent-circumstances exception did not justify opening a closed metal box after suspects were secured. Search exceeded emergency scope and required suppression.
DLRA exclusion turns on conviction of enumerated serious offenses, not on persistent-felony-offender status alone. Resentencing eligibility remains where no disqualifying conviction exists.
People failed to justify additional excludable delay under CPL 30.30(4)(a). Statutory speedy-trial dismissal by Criminal Court was reinstated.
Questioning after counsel disclaimed continued representation did not violate New York right-to-counsel protections. Police could proceed absent active representation on the matter.
Ineffective-assistance challenge based on omitted adverse-inference charge failed on direct record. Counsel's decision was not shown to be devoid of strategic explanation.
Retained-counsel ineffectiveness claims did not establish deprivation of meaningful representation. Conviction affirmed because alleged errors were either strategic or nonprejudicial.
Suppression and evidentiary challenges in the controlled-buy prosecution were rejected. County Court order affirmed.

Penal Law 220.25(2) close-proximity presumption did not apply after defendant exited the apartment and entered a vehicle without immediate-flight proof. Mischarge required reversal of the affected possession counts and a new trial on those counts.

Plea-voluntariness challenge to unannounced PRS term was reviewable without preservation in these circumstances. Plea vacatur required because defendant lacked constitutionally adequate notice at plea.

Admission of certain prior consistent statements and exclusion of proposed impeachment testimony fell within trial-court discretion. Evidentiary rulings did not constitute reversible bolstering error.
Issues raised on appeal did not establish reversible error. Appellate Division order affirmed.
Guilty plea was invalid because record lacked a constitutionally sufficient allocution of rights waiver. Plea vacated and accusatory instrument dismissed.
Conditional confinement to compel testimony was civil-coercive rather than criminal-punitive on this record. Subsequent Penal Law contempt prosecution was not barred by double jeopardy.
Miranda warnings were ineffective where prefatory language diluted and contradicted core rights advisements. Suppression required because defendants were not clearly informed before waiver.
Appeal dismissed for failure to satisfy CPL 450.90(2)(a). Jurisdictional predicate for Court of Appeals review was absent.

Right-to-counsel claim arising from pro se guilty plea was cognizable under CPL 440.10 despite omission on direct appeal. Procedural bar did not apply because the claim implicated the plea's constitutional validity.
Post-Miranda silence evidence was improperly admitted under an erroneous open-door theory. New trial required because constitutional error was not harmless.
Claims advanced on appeal did not warrant disturbance of the judgment. Appellate Division order affirmed.
Sentencing challenge to deviation from conditional promise was unpreserved under CPL 470.05. Affirmance followed because no reviewable issue remained.

Repugnancy analysis in hate-crime pairings is controlled by the charge as given, not by trial evidence. Non-hate offense functions as a lesser included of the corresponding hate offense; inconsistent verdict required modification with leave to re-present.

Failure to provide meaningful notice and response to substantive jury notes under CPL 310.30/O'Rama is mode-of-proceedings error. New-trial relief was required where the record did not show compliance before verdict acceptance.

Anonymous 911 tip and police corroboration supplied reasonable suspicion for the Argyris/DiSalvo stop. Johnson stop lacked sufficient reliability and legal authority, requiring suppression and dismissal.
Issues challenging the sex-offense conviction did not establish reversible error. Appellate Division order affirmed.
Duplicity challenge based on trial proof must be preserved when indictment is facially single-act. Unpreserved claim was not reviewable and remaining issues failed.
Search-incident doctrine did not apply where arrest would not have occurred absent contraband found during the search. Suppression and indictment dismissal were required.

CPL 440.10(1)(g) newly-discovered-evidence denials are reviewable for abuse of discretion under a developed record. Summary denial was improper because mtDNA exclusion evidence warranted a hearing-stage evaluation.
District Court judgments against the corporate defendant were properly reinstated. Appellate Term reversal lacked a sustainable legal basis.
Reasonable-suspicion determination was a mixed question of law and fact supported by record evidence. Further review was unavailable and affirmance followed.

Questioning a represented defendant about an unrelated crime after counsel-entry violations breached New York right-to-counsel protections in the circumstances presented. Statements were suppressed and a new trial ordered.
CPL 330.30(1) motions cannot rely on facts outside the trial record. Post-verdict claims premised on extra-record material were procedurally improper.
